summary: Bodies keep one identity through the features that change them. src/domain/cad/cadBodies.ts derives the bodies after each feature from the history and each kind's declared body behaviour. A body is keyed by the feature that created it, plus an occurrence where that feature makes a copy or a piece: inst(i,j) for a pattern copy, split(k) for a piece of a split body and mirror for a mirror image. A feature that modifies a body (fillet, chamfer, shell, move, cut, join, pocket and the patterns) keeps its key and is recorded in modifiedBy. A Boolean keeps its target's key and records itself as consumedBy on each tool. Each state is { key, kind, createdBy, modifiedBy, consumedBy?, pieces?, ambiguous?, untracked? }. Validation and the kernel resolve a stored target through this lineage, strictly by the feature whose result the body now is, as before, so every diagnostic is unchanged. The kernel keys its bodies by body key and tracks the parts of a body, its split pieces and separate pattern copies, only where continuity is certain. Each solid of a feature's result is traced to every source solid it keeps a face of unchanged: the target's pieces, each pattern copy and a fused tool. A face two solids or two sources share is never traced, since which of them it would count for follows the kernel's order. A solid that continues one target piece keeps its key, a copy is inst(i,j) of the piece copied, and a piece split again is split(q), numbered by the first face it keeps, never by position, size or centroid. Anything else gets a fresh feature/split(k) key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess. Faces rank in the order the kernel lists solids, so ranks order solids only when the faces they are numbered by lie in the same solid of one source and differ; solids that equal ranks or the kernel's order would order are ambiguous. A solid keeping no face of the body may be a piece of any of its keys, so it, the keys continued by one solid and the keys no solid continues are ambiguous together. A mirror image starts whole under its own key. Ambiguity is kept in groups and carries to every descendant: the keys descending from one group through one source form a group, an ambiguous key resolves only among the current pieces of its group, and a key ambiguous only by descent extends the issue that reported its ambiguity instead of being reported again, until that issue lists 4,096 keys; the later feature then reports the rest in an issue of its own. Since the kernel's order picked which member's key each solid continued, a group keeps every former member's key, whether its solid split, was copied or went, while a solid descends from the group through the target, and a key no body lists resolves as ambiguous when another kernel order would have given it to the descendant of a member of an ambiguous group. A consumed body's ambiguous keys resolve as missing with the Boolean that consumed it. CadBuildResult.bodyIssues reports each feature's ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts and untracked-body-parts, with more-body-issues past 512: a hook D1 can adopt. Every build returns the body states (CadBuildResult.bodies, CadMesh.bodyKey), and the worker reply check verifies them against the meshes. Consumers choose bodies by key: a command started with a feature selected (Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket and the target of a Boolean) and File > Section for CAM now act on the body that feature leads to, wherever it sits in that body's history, instead of falling back to the latest body. The DXF export dialog's initial body is chosen the same way, and cad_build rows add bodyKey. Stored targets still hold feature ids and nothing stored changes. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata shapes and their resolution are defined and tested but not stored. docs/maintainers/cad-features.md describes body identity.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. The CAD document and edit schemas, agent tool schemas and descriptions, parsed documents, diagnostics, kernel geometry, sections, STL exports and saved bytes in the browser cache and folder adapters are identical to main at 9b236720 (0.0.796), this change's base. Two additive changes are visible. cad_build body rows gain a bodyKey field beside featureId, which agents may ignore; tools still take featureId as bodyId. With a feature selected that is no longer the latest state of its body, such as a pad that was later filleted, starting Fillet, Chamfer, Move, a pattern, Mirror, Pocket or a Boolean, or opening File > Section for CAM, now targets that pad's body in its filleted state instead of the most recently changed body.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage or journal change. The published CAD document schema, edit schema and every feature variant are byte-identical. Body keys are derived on every rebuild and never stored; stored target, source and tool fields still hold feature ids. The worker build reply gains optional bodies, bodyIssues and CadMesh.bodyKey fields. The main thread and the worker ship together, and the reply check accepts a reply without them, as older build results are. When present, it requires one body state per mesh, in mesh order, whose key is the mesh's bodyKey, whose current feature is the mesh's featureId and whose pieces, when present, key the mesh's solids one for one with no key repeated, and whose ambiguous groups, when present, are non-empty and share no key; it requires unique mesh keys and at most 512 issues. Review round 2 changed ambiguous from a list of keys to a list of groups; it is part of the build reply only, which the main thread and the worker ship together, and is never stored. A list of part keys holds at most 4,096 keys, and an issue message gives counts, never part keys. A body with more parts, or a longer part key, is reported as untracked, so a large valid model is summarised, never refused. Post engine API remains 1, saved-job engine remains 3 and CAD_PRECISION_VERSION stays 2. S8's CadBodyRef and CadBodyMetadata are types and resolution functions only.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation, input-version or WebMCP guard change. Initial CAD discovery stays at 51,178 of its 51,200 UTF-8 bytes: no tool name, description or input schema changes. cad_describe_features and cad_describe_edits return byte-identical replies. cad_build body rows add bodyKey, the creating feature id with any occurrence (such as flip/mirror), after featureId; docs/site/agents.md explains it. Every diagnostic code and message is unchanged. The only new codes, ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues, are body issues returned in bodyIssues, never diagnostics.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change and no new application controls. Commands started with a feature selected now choose that feature's body by key; with no selection, or a selection that leads to no drawn body, they choose the latest body as before. The Boolean tool default is the latest other body, as before.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Kernel geometry, mesh order, previews, sections and STL exports are byte-identical. STEP export writes the same bodies in the same order under the same names, the feature names, until S8 stores body metadata.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Every parity document loads, validates, rebuilds and saves to identical bytes through both the browser cache and folder adapters.
checklist.verification: Parity, against main at 9b236720 (0.0.796), the base of this change, captured on that tree and on this branch merged with it, with the same results as against main at 5ab4b5ea (0.0.795) before the merge, again at d68b4cf2 after review round 2 and at d2981d2e after review round 3: agent tool metadata (51,178 bytes), the cad_describe_features and cad_describe_edits replies, the document and edit schemas are byte-identical. So are, over 86 documents (the 17 kernel parity models, the 6 benchmark steps, 41 sketch fixture parts and 22 body histories of modifying features, Booleans, nested patterns, mirrors, splits and suppression), parsed documents, validation, feature inputs and dependencies, parameter inspection and the bytes each document saves, loads and saves again through the browser cache and folder adapters (172 saves). So are the codes and messages of 3,578 diagnostics from mutated variants of them: suppression toggles, deletions, features moved first or last, every id field retargeted or cleared, changed operations and a Boolean tool pointed at its own target. Over the same 86 documents, every kernel build fingerprint, diagnostic, mesh (positions, indices, face and edge groups, with the random per-build topology keys numbered by first appearance), section, topology descriptor and STL export is identical; the kernel parity snapshot test passes unchanged. The kernel's body states equal the domain lineage for every kernel parity model, and each build reply passes the worker reply check. Identity tests: src/domain/cad/__tests__/cadBodies.test.ts (48 tests) covers keys and their text form, the lineage of every body behaviour, suppression, reorder and delete, the body parts each kind of kernel fact gives (piece ranks, ranks of faces in different solids, equal ranks, solids keeping no face as possible splits and possible pieces of any key, merges, losses, the bridge and island, inherited ambiguity in groups per copy, kept while its group survives, through splits and copies of its members, and extending its first issue up to the list limit, pattern copies separate, merged, nested and vanished, limits and overflow, issue messages and the issue cap), modifier histories shared by 3,000 states, the S8 reference and metadata resolution with ambiguous keys resolved within their group, keys another kernel order would have given resolved as ambiguous and consumed ambiguous keys resolved with their consumer, selection by key and the checks of values received from the worker, including repeated keys and malformed groups. src/features/cad/kernel/cadKernelBodies.test.ts (27 tests, in the kernel) covers keys through fillet, chamfer, shell, move, pocket, cut, join and Boolean, pattern copies and mirror keys, piece numbering by kept faces for three cut positions built twice each (the right piece is split(0) although the kernel lists it second), pieces through a move, a second split and a joined island, an ambiguous cleave, the five review round 1 repros, review round 2's mirror, partial-provenance, per-copy resolution and inherited-issue repros, one half of an ambiguous cleave cut away, review round 3's face two solids share and ambiguous piece split again, each in both solid orders, replies whose pieces do not match their solids or repeat a key, and a property test over random histories, aiming splits at ambiguous pieces, that builds every step in both solid orders and requires every key either order lists to resolve with the same status in both. A workbench test checks that selecting a filleted pad sends Section for CAM and Move to the pad's body and not to a later block. Mutations, each alone against the identity suites, the kernel parity test and the workbench test, all 16 caught on aa2696b9; the two the workbench test catches fail the same tests on the merged tree. The four from before review, rerun after round 1: a modifying feature minting its own key fails 33 tests (12 domain, 20 kernel, 1 workbench); a Boolean keeping its tool's key fails 4; selection falling back to the latest body by position fails 2; split pieces ordered by centroid fail 4 kernel tests. Twelve break the inheritance rule or the reply limits: a tool-only island taking a piece no solid continues (3), a solid keeping no face taking a piece left over by elimination (3), a merged solid keeping the first target key (4), ambiguity not inherited (4), losses not reported (8), unidentifiable pieces dropped instead of left ambiguous (2), pieces carried over whenever the solid count is unchanged (6), a whole body splitting only when the count grows (1), the ambiguity message listing every key (2), parts not capped at 4,096 (1), pattern copies' faces not recorded (4) and a join's tool faces not traced (2). The random-history property test alone catches seven of the twelve; it first missed the inherited-ambiguity mutation and now checks that every piece keeping or extending an ambiguous key stays ambiguous. Round 2 adds nine, each alone against the same suites at d68b4cf2, all caught (the workbench test catches none, as none touches selection): ranks of faces in different solids of one source ordering solids (4: two domain tests, the kernel mirror permutation and the random-history test); a solid keeping no face not counting as a possible split (2); a piece continued by one solid staying certain beside a solid keeping no face (2); the descendants of a group through different copies sharing one group (4); an ambiguous key resolving among every ambiguous piece of its body (2); inherited ambiguity reported again as a new cause (3); a state made again on every request, copying the history (1); repeated piece keys accepted (2); and an ambiguous piece reported lost while a solid of its group is left (4, including the random-history test). Round 3 adds eight, each alone against the same suites at d2981d2e, all caught: a face two solids of a source share traced to the first (1: the kernel shared-face test); a face two sources share traced to the first (1: the same test); equal ranks ordering solids (1: the domain equal-rank test); members continued under other keys leaving their group (8: four domain tests, the kernel large pattern, per-copy resolution and split ambiguous piece tests, and the random-history test); members leaving once every earlier piece split, the first round 3 rule (7, including the random-history test); keys another kernel order would have given resolving as missing (3, including the random-history test); a consumed body's ambiguous keys losing their consumer (1); and keys past a full issue dropped (1: the domain issue limit test). Since review round 1. All five findings are fixed in aa2696b9 under one rule: a key is inherited only when continuity is certain; anything else gets a fresh key, a reported ambiguity or a reported loss, never a guess. createCadKernelFaceSources replaces cadKernelSolidOrigins and records the faces of every source a feature combines (the target's solids, each pattern copy before it is released, and a fused tool); cadBodyParts gives each result solid its key from the source solids it keeps faces of. occurrences is removed: pattern copies are traced per solid into pieces. ambiguous-split-order is replaced by ambiguous-body-parts, lost-body-parts, untracked-body-parts and more-body-issues. (1) A valid build failed the worker check because the ambiguity message listed every key (9,721 characters). Messages now give counts and keep the keys in pieces; lists hold at most 4,096 keys, past which a body is reported untracked; issues stop at 512 with a summary; modifiedBy stays uncapped and checked by entry; and the reply check requires pieces to key the mesh's solids one for one. 100 copies of a cleaved rod created by a 36-character UUID id give 200 ambiguous keys, a 123-character message and a reply that passes the check. (2) An island joined beside a split box inherited a piece's key by elimination. Every solid is now traced to every predecessor it keeps faces of: the island gets bridge/split(0), the bridged solid bridge/split(1), and both box pieces are reported lost and resolve as missing. (3) A pocket in one piece of a cleaved cylinder erased its ambiguity. Ambiguity now carries to every descendant, and the pieces stay ambiguous candidates. (4) A pattern copy cut away still resolved. Copies are traced per solid, so the cut reports box/inst(1,0) lost and it resolves as missing. (5) A cut that split one patterned cube and removed the other went unseen because the count did not change. Splits and losses are found per predecessor solid, never by totals; the repro gives box/inst(0,0)/split(0) and split(1) and reports box/inst(1,0) lost. Each repro is a kernel test, and a property test over random histories (10 seeds of 5 steps from a box or disc, drawing patterns, one- to three-slot splits, cuts, one- or two-profile joins and pockets) checks at every step that no key repeats, that each piece keeps or extends a key from before or is a fresh key of the step's feature, that a solid inheriting a key without ambiguity overlaps its predecessor, that ambiguity is reported and inherited, that no piece vanishes unreported, that every reported loss resolves as missing then and later, and that rebuilds are identical. The kernel gives kept faces cheaply but not faces a Boolean's simplification merges: an extruded circle's two half side faces are merged by a pattern's fuse, so the copies of round hole and boss patterns keep no face and get fresh, ambiguous keys instead of guessed ones until K3 provides the Boolean's own face history. Parity after round 1 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, against main at 5ab4b5ea and again after the merge against main at 9b236720; derived body states or issues changed from round 0 in 18 of the 86 documents, all as the rule requires. S5 (0.0.796, #111) is on main as 9b236720 and f99219ca merges it, keeping 0.0.797 with previousVersion 0.0.796. Only the version fields of package.json and package-lock.json conflicted; CadWorkbench.tsx, its test and docs/site/agents.md merged cleanly, and on the merged tree the body states and issues equal those before the merge. Since review round 2. All six findings are fixed in d68b4cf2, and nothing stored changes. (1) A mirror image took its source's piece order as certain: reversing the first cleave's solid order moved flip/mirror/split(0) to another piece of a cleaved, patterned, mirrored and cut cylinder. Faces rank within their source in the order the kernel lists its solids, so ranks now order solids only when the faces they are numbered by lie in the same solid of one source. A mirror image still starts whole under its own key; when a later feature splits it, the pieces numbered by faces of different solids of the image are ambiguous, and the piece keeping no face of it is numbered last in either order. It does not carry its source's pieces: mapping source keys onto image keys would be a second naming scheme, and the rank rule already refuses any order the kernel decides. (2) Incomplete face provenance counted as proof: an intersection that kept an end slab and an interior core of the first of two solids left the body whole, and with a patterned target kept box/inst(0,0) certain. A solid keeping no face of the body now counts as a possible split whatever the totals, and as a possible piece of any key, so it, the keys continued by one solid and the keys no solid continues are ambiguous together: the repro reports keep/split(0), box/inst(0,0) and box/inst(1,0) as one group, and a whole two-solid body cut the same way splits into multi/split(0) and multi/split(1). (3) Ambiguous references resolved across pattern occurrences. CadBodyState.ambiguous now holds groups: the keys that descend from one group through one source form a group, and an ambiguous key resolves only among the current pieces of its group, so rod/split(0)/inst(0,0) resolves among its own copy's two pieces. A group's keys that no solid continues stay in it while a solid descends from it through the target, and are lost after, so cutting away one half of the cleaved rod leaves both keys ambiguous to the half left instead of one lost and one certain. (4) Inherited ambiguity was reported again by each later feature. A key ambiguous only because it descends from an ambiguous key now extends the issue that reported that key: 100 copies of the cleaved rod give one cleave issue of 202 keys. (5) Every modifier copied the body's modifier list. Modifiers now link into a history the states share, and modifiedBy is made once, when a state is asked for; validation only asks whether a body exists. (6) The worker check accepted repeated piece keys. It now rejects a key repeated in pieces or across ambiguous groups, an empty group and a flat list, with malformed-reply tests in both suites. The random-history test now also draws mirrors and Boolean intersections with one or two blocks through or inside the body, aims cuts at a single piece and joins across two, runs 16 seeds, and builds every step a second time with the kernel's multi-solid Boolean results listed in reverse: every key must name the same solid, by its box and surface area, in both orders, or be ambiguous in both, and the issues must agree. Parity after round 2 against main at 9b236720 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, and tool metadata stays at 51,178 bytes. Derived body data changed from round 1 in 4 of the 86 documents: plate-40-pattern reports one ambiguity of 50 keys instead of two issues of 10 and 40, and near-full-turn-pattern, split-fillet and split-cylinder keep the same ambiguous keys as one group. Since review round 3. All four findings are fixed in 27c90694, 4bd71755 and d2981d2e, and nothing stored changes. (1) Equal face ranks certified kernel-dependent identities: two adjacent native solids sharing a face, intersected by a slab spanning their boundary, both traced to that face, so reversing the solid order swapped imported/split(0) between x = 8 to 10 and x = 10 to 12. A face that two solids of a source, or two sources, share is now never traced, since which of them it would count for follows the order they are listed in, and solids that equal ranks would order are ambiguous. The repro, built from boxes fused by the builder algorithm, traces no face and is ambiguous in both orders. It is tested at the kernel and domain boundary only, since a STEP round trip did not keep the shared face. (2) Splitting an ambiguous member made its old key missing: after a box split at x = 18 to 20, filleted on every edge and split again at x = 30 to 32, round/split(1) became missing although it could name the unsplit left piece, and reversing the first cut's solid order swapped which key disappeared. Since the kernel's order picked which member's key each solid continued, a group now keeps every former member's key, whether its solid split, was copied or went, while a solid descends from the group through the target. Keeping it only while another member was left unchanged, the first fix, still depended on the order: with splits aimed at ambiguous pieces, the random-history test found a key ambiguous in one order and missing in the other. A key no body lists resolves as ambiguous when its nearest listed ancestor is ambiguous and another member of that ancestor's group has a descendant by the same steps, which another kernel order would have given it. After a pattern, the old keys of an ambiguous group therefore resolve as ambiguous among the original's pieces instead of missing. The either-order helper now requires every key either order lists to resolve with the same status in both, and the generator adds a slot through the middle of an ambiguous piece. (3) Consumed ambiguous keys lost their consumer: a key kept only in its group resolved as plain missing once a Boolean consumed the body. The consumed lookup now includes ambiguous groups and the keys resolved as above, so both halves of a cleaved rod resolve as missing with consumedBy union. (4) The issue limit was not documented. A key ambiguous by descent extends its first issue only until that issue lists 4,096 keys; the later feature reports the rest in an ambiguous-body-parts issue of its own, as the guide, this record and the pull request now say. A domain test runs a comb cut's 1,000 ambiguous teeth through two patterns with a cut between them: the comb's issue fills to 4,096 keys and the second pattern reports the other 904. Parity after round 3 against main at 9b236720 is byte-identical in everything stored, diagnosed or built, and tool metadata stays at 51,178 bytes. Derived body data is the same as after round 2 in all 86 documents, none of which has a case the round 3 rules change. Timing, against main at 9b236720, by minimums of back-to-back main and branch runs with the tree order alternating; an overlapping run is noted by the number of two-second samples in which another checkout ran a test, build, type check or benchmark. Worker reply check (isCadKernelReply on captured build replies, four clean pairs): the large pattern's reply, whose 200 ambiguous parts make the largest body state here, costs 948 to 1,189 µs (+25%) against a build of about 6 s; all 24 replies 2,438 to 2,766 µs (+13.5%), three quarters of it the large pattern; plate-hole-pattern 1.1% more, gear-and-plate 372.3 to 372.4 µs and box-fillet-all-edges within noise. Rebuild (benchmark-cad, four pairs; pair 2 clean, pair 3 branch busy 29 and main 3, pair 4 main busy 110, and in pair 1 main's gear-and-plate steps ran 2.4 to 2.9 times slower with nothing else seen): build and shipped edit stay within 2% either way, plate-hole-pattern build 62.89 to 61.56 ms and edit 59.13 to 58.88 ms, gear-and-plate build 419.72 to 418.76 ms and edit 427.14 to 420.75 ms, box-fillet-all-edges build 35.43 to 35.66 ms and edit 34.84 to 34.48 ms; checking and cloning the reply on the main thread stay within noise, as do the drag preview and viewport reference measures. An earlier set of four pairs, run while another checkout type-checked and ran end-to-end tests, was about three times slower for both trees and is not used. The worker reply check and rebuild figures were measured on round 1's merged tree and were not re-timed in round 2, which re-timed document load alone. Review round 3 changed neither document load nor the reply check, so nothing was re-timed. Document load, re-timed at d68b4cf2 (parse and validation, 60 runs per measure, four clean pairs): 2,000 chained transforms of one body 12.96 to 13.80 ms (+0.84 ms, +6.5%, paired ratios 1.031 to 1.084), where review round 2 measured 14.46 to 19.07 ms before modifier histories were shared. A separate three-way run (three clean rounds) gives +0.38, +0.56 and +1.43 ms over main for 1,000, 2,000 and 4,000 modifiers, about 0.36 µs per modifier and linear; skipping histories altogether during validation leaves 7.48, 13.24 and 24.97 ms against 7.50, 13.22 and 25.14 ms with shared histories, so the remainder is the lineage's per-feature lookups, not the histories. 32 sketches 49.90 to 49.41 ms (paired ratios 0.970 to 1.024), so round 1's +2.4% does not recur; 32 extruded sketches 54.73 to 55.06 ms; 8 extruded sketches 13.40 to 13.36 ms; a dependent sketch 3.09 to 3.03 ms; the 23 parity and benchmark documents 13.42 to 13.54 ms (paired median 1.017). Pointer moves: hovering a plane renders the workbench again. Main recomputes the visible-body set on every render. This branch derives the lineage once per document, the drawn body ids once per build and the Section for CAM body once per selection, so pointer moves recompute no body list. Deriving the lineage of all 23 documents takes 0.05 ms against 0.01 ms for main's visible set, about 2 µs per document, once per document version. Bundle, production builds of main at 9b236720 and this branch at d2981d2e: the kernel worker grows from 770,644 to 781,016 bytes (+10,372, +4,421 gzipped) for the lineage, the face sources and the reply checks; round 1 added 2,759 bytes of it, round 2 2,291 and round 3 103. The shared CAD chunk with the feature definitions now also holds the lineage and is emitted as two preloaded chunks, cadFeatureInputs (54,569 bytes) and cadParameters (6,104 bytes), instead of one of 50,415 bytes: +10,258 bytes, +4,105 gzipped, and one more small request on first load. The worker client grows by 579 bytes and every other chunk by 1 to 158 bytes. All JavaScript and CSS grow by 21,760 bytes (0.36%), 8,999 gzipped (0.51%). Checks at d2981d2e: the focused suites pass (164 files and 2,220 tests: src/domain/cad, src/features/cad/kernel, the workbench test and the site tool tests, including cadBodies.test.ts with 48 and cadKernelBodies.test.ts with 27); the app type check passes; npm run build passes, including the documentation build and check and the corresponding-source checks; npm run lint has zero findings over 628 source files; npm run ui:check passes; check-release passes on its own and against origin/main with this record; the branch and title pass the pull request naming check. The full Vitest run last ran locally on round 1's merged tree (632 files, 7,356 tests), and the pull request's continuous integration runs it again at this head. Specs, run in round 1, each alone with two workers against the merged tree's production build while the end-to-end port was free: cad-workflow including Section for CAM and sending the section to CAM (32), cad-kernel (2), cad-topology-repick (3), cad-region-workflow (1), cad-intersecting-areas (1), cad-plane-selection-section (6) and project-navigation with saved CAD, reload and STEP export (2), 47 tests, all pass. cad-kernel, cad-region-workflow, cad-topology-repick and cad-workflow check cad_build body rows through the agent tools. They were not rerun locally in review rounds 2 and 3, whose changes are in the lineage, the face tracer and the reply check; the pull request's continuous integration runs every browser journey. publicNotes.summary: CAD bodies keep their identity through the features that change them.
changes: With a feature selected, Fillet, Chamfer, Move, the patterns, Mirror, Pocket, Boolean and Section for CAM act on the body that feature belongs to, even after later features changed it.
CAD build results for agents name each body by the feature that created it (bodyKey), which stays the same through later changes.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
